The problem
Data is everywhere. But without Lens, it's like trying to read without your glasses. Blurry. Unclear. Out of focus.

The data exists. It always has. What hasn't is a way to connect it all and surface what matters.

Lens works from day one with what you have. Every additional source makes the intelligence richer and the answers sharper. You decide the pace.

Competitive landscape

AI is everywhere.
Context is still fragmented.

The market has moved quickly. Workday, Oracle, Visier, Glean, Moveworks, Microsoft and others now offer powerful assistants, agents and analytics. Lens is not betting that nobody else will build AI. It is designed to connect the context between specialist systems and make it useful across the organisation.

CategoryExamplesWhat they already do wellWhere Lens aims to add value
Enterprise AI & agentsGlean · Microsoft CopilotCompany knowledge, enterprise context, search, agents and cross-application work.Connect that broad work context with workforce, commercial demand, external market signals and decision history.

HCM-native AIWorkday / Sana · Oracle HCM AgentsDeep HR data, employee self-service, people workflows, embedded agents and increasingly sophisticated analysis.Sit above the HCM rather than inside one ecosystem, joining HR context with CRM, projects, finance, market and other systems.

External talent intelligenceLinkedIn Talent Insights · Lightcast · Revelio LabsLabour-market supply, skills, hiring, movement and competitor signals.Connect the external market to the organisation's real internal capacity, hiring pipeline and future commercial demand.

Start small

Meet your current challenges, then expand.

A 30-person startup doesn't need the same Lens as a 30,000-person enterprise.

A Lens pilot aims to solve one challenge at a time. No transformation programme. No requirement to replace your existing systems. Add steps, only when needed.

1
Be productive.
Employee questions, onboarding, screen guidance, workforce visibility, hiring risk, commercial capacity or leadership intelligence. Start where the pain is real.
2
Connect what you already have
Policies, documents, spreadsheets, HR systems, ATS, CRM, project data or external sources. Lens can begin simply and become richer as more sources are connected.
3
Configure Lens around your business
We shape the experience, permissions, context and outputs around your people, processes and priorities rather than forcing you into a fixed implementation.
4
Run it with real users
Put Lens into everyday use with a focused group and measure what matters: time saved, questions resolved, friction removed, insight quality or better decisions.
5
Expand only if it earns the right
Add more users, systems, workflows and intelligence as the value becomes clear. The pilot should create the evidence for what comes next.
